title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-03
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: SO 0018 오늘 터미널 마감 전 트럭·HAWB·지연 사유 서면 확인, 실사 결과 법인장 보고 준비, Mai 3건 한 통 재촉. 지난주 시험 7/20점(정답률 35%, 10/31 채점 완료). 월 07:08 실행분이라 월요일 메일 미반영.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Tuesday, November third. This is your English briefing for the drive to work.
This script was written early on Monday morning. So some items may already be closed by the time you hear this. Please check Monday's emails when you arrive.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three. Part two is the reports to collect. Part three is the replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is the English review. Part six is a role-play. Part seven is a short practice with your weak words. Part eight is the closing.
Let's start.
Part one. Top three for today.
Number one is the Vince air shipment, S O six three four, ending in zero zero one eight. It has six hundred fifteen pieces in two hanger boxes.

Here is what happened. The first plan was a flight on November first. Then the forwarder, Hecny, said that flight was not possible. Hecny said the typhoon had pushed back flights from Da Nang. On Saturday, Hecny sent a new air booking. The cut-off time at the V I A G S air terminal is today, November third.

Why does it matter? The required delivery date was October thirtieth, so this shipment is already late. If it misses today's cut-off, the delay gets longer. The buyer may also ask who pays for any extra cost. So far, no email says who is responsible.
Your first action is simple. Before nine o'clock, ask Ms Trinh Do three things. Has the truck left? Has she checked the draft house air waybill? Does Hecny confirm the delay reason in writing?
Here is the sentence to use. "Please confirm that the truck has left and the boxes will arrive before the cut-off."
Number two is the result of the fabric and thread physical count. The count was on Saturday, October thirty-first. Ms Nga sent the accounting team's file that afternoon.

Why does it matter? Mr Moon knows the count took place. He also sent a customs balance file to Mr Logan Kim on Sunday night, and you were on copy. So head office is looking at the same stock from another side. Your count result should be ready before anyone asks for it.

Your first action is to open Ms Nga's file. Find the rows where the Q R system and the actual stock are different. Then decide which rows need a correction in the system. After that, send Mr Moon a short report. Keep it to the total rows checked, the rows that were different, and the next step.

Number three is the late work from Mai in purchasing. There are three items. The first is the e-ticket for Mr Asanka. The second is the consumables ledger update, which was due on October twenty-ninth. The third is the new quotes for the thirty-nine relaxing racks, which were due on October twenty-eighth.
I found no email from Mai on any of these three items since Saturday morning. Mai may have replied on Zalo, so please check there first.
Why does it matter? Mr Asanka lands on November tenth. You need to check that the name on the ticket matches his passport. The rack quotes are also holding up your report to Mr Moon.

Your first action is to send Mai one message with one deadline. Do not send three separate messages. Here is the sentence. "Just a reminder that the e-ticket is due by ten o'clock today. The ledger and quotes are due by three o'clock."
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, Mr Sateesh. Kasun from Aritzia visited on Friday and sent product review feedback on Sunday. The email says the panel attaching needs more attention because a lot of unevenness was observed. Kasun asked Mr Sateesh to work on it. Please check what action the Q A team has taken. Also remember that the sewing manager position is empty until Mr Asanka starts.
Here is the sentence to use. "When will you be able to share the action plan for the panel attaching issue?"

Second, Ms An. There are two things to check. The first is the test date for the new fusing chemical, SEVICH. Van said it would be on the November third consumables list. The second is the result of the first Sunday of electrical lug replacement. That work was planned for November first, and the second day is November eighth.
Here is the sentence. "Please let me know the test date, and please share the result and photos of the lug work from Sunday."

Third, Mr Mai, the maintenance manager. Your daily report said the maintenance team would clean the fusing machine belt on Sunday, with three people. Please check that it was done, and whether the belt looks better. He also confirmed that thirty sandbags are enough for three doors. Rain is expected until November fourth, so this is a good week to test that answer.
Here is the sentence. "Please send me a photo of the belt after cleaning. Please also tell me if you observed any leaks."

Fourth, Ms Ly in H R. The October working hours had to go into the E R P by eleven o'clock on Monday. Hannah Kim at head office set that deadline. Please check it was entered on time. Ms Ly also sent the list of employees returning from maternity leave in November.
Here is the sentence. "Could you confirm whether the October working hours were entered before the deadline?"

Fifth, Thao in I E. On Friday you asked for a recheck of the I E target for Aritzia style four eight five seven zero. Please check for a reply. Remember, this Thao is the I E Thao, not Ms Thao in M R.
Here is the sentence. "I'm following up on the I E target check for style four eight five seven zero."
Part three. Replies you owe.

First, Ms Trinh Do on the ExIm Ledger. She replied on Saturday evening. She said they corrected the errors and asked you to check again. Do not close this on her word. Open the file and count three things. How many rows still show TO CHECK? Are the September costs filled in? Did she answer your two questions? You also saw that her team sent the January to June logistics data to Mr Cris Jang on Saturday.
Your first sentence could be this. "Thank you for the update. I checked the file again, and here is what remains."

Second, Mr Chamin. His last day was October thirty-first. His email about the air ticket and baggage from October twenty-ninth still has no email reply on record. The certificate for his personal income tax will come after the payment on November fifth. Ms Trinh Tran in accounting confirmed this on Saturday, and she will send it to him by email.
Your first sentence could be this. "Please note that accounting will send your tax certificate by email after the payment on November fifth."

Third, Ms Nga on the manager salary file. Your memo says you still need to correct the guidance you gave her about which version is the basis. Please do this before the salary payment. This is her first month preparing this work, so a clear answer helps.
Your first sentence could be this. "I'd like to clarify which file you should use for the actual payment."
Fourth, Ms An and Mr Mai on the sandbags. You asked how many bags were filled and where they are. They answered that thirty bags are enough. A short reply is all you need.
Your first sentence could be this. "Thank you. Thirty bags is fine. Please place them as soon as heavy rain is expected."
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.
There is nothing on your Outlook calendar for today.
Today, Tuesday, is the needle order for Chloe Kim at head office. It goes for approval on Wednesday.
Tomorrow, Wednesday, November fourth, is the deadline for the party room lock with Ms Tho. Wednesday is also the production consumables day. Remember, Van sends that report. You only give your okay.

Thursday, November fifth, is salary payment day. That includes Mr Chamin's final settlement. The monthly labor cost report to Mr Moon is also due around this date. The electricity results are due between the third and the fifth.
Saturday, November seventh, has a salary report on your calendar. It is also the day for the manager salary data and the purchase cost list for head office.
A little further out, Mr Asanka arrives on November tenth. The V A T refund application is planned for the same day.
Part five. English review.
We start with three new items from Monday's card. Then we go back to words that were wrong on the Saturday test.

The expression is reconcile. It means to check two sets of data against each other. For example, we will reconcile the Q R stock with the physical count. Now say it with me. Reconcile. ... ... ... One more time. We will reconcile the Q R stock with the physical count. ... ... ...

The expression is sufficient. It means enough, in a more formal way. For example, thirty sandbags are sufficient for the three locations. Now say it with me. Sufficient. ... ... ... One more time. Thirty sandbags are sufficient for the three locations. ... ... ...

The expression is as far as I can see. Use it when you point out a problem without being too strong. For example, as far as I can see, the September costs are still empty in the ledger. Now say it with me. As far as I can see, the costs are still empty. ... ... ... One more time. As far as I can see, the costs are still empty. ... ... ...

The expression is accurate. It means correct in every detail. For example, please check that the Vietnamese text in the letter is accurate. Now say it with me. Accurate. ... ... ... One more time. Please check that the numbers are accurate. ... ... ...

The expression is justify. It means to give a good reason for something. For example, please justify the purchase of three units. Now say it with me. Justify. ... ... ... One more time. Please justify the purchase of three units. ... ... ...

The expression is address. Here it is a verb. It means to deal with a problem or a question. For example, only question number one has been addressed so far. Now say it with me. Address. ... ... ... One more time. Please address the panel issue first. ... ... ...

The expression is clarify. It means to make something clear. It is different from verify. Verify means to check that something is correct. For example, please clarify who enters the lot number. Now say it with me. Clarify. ... ... ... One more time. Please clarify who enters the lot number. ... ... ...

The expression is in case. It tells someone what to do if something happens. For example, in case the power goes out, please start the generator. Now say it with me. In case the rain is heavy, please use the sandbags. ... ... ... One more time. In case the rain is heavy, please use the sandbags. ... ... ...

The expression is we have decided to, instead of. After the word of, use the i n g form. For example, we have decided to replace four drives instead of replacing all thirteen. Now say it with me. We have decided to repair the machine instead of buying a new one. ... ... ... One more time. We have decided to repair the machine instead of buying a new one. ... ... ...

The expression is rather than. After it, say what you do not want. Then say what you do want. For example, rather than forwarding the email to others, please check it yourself. Now say it with me. Rather than calling me, please send one list at the end of the day. ... ... ... One more time. Rather than calling me, please send one list at the end of the day. ... ... ...
Part six. Role-play.
The situation is this. You are reporting the Vince air shipment to Mr Moon. Listen first.
Mr Moon says: Mr Lee, what is happening with the Vince shipment?
Anthony says: Sir, the required delivery date was October thirtieth, so we are already late. The new cut-off is today.
Mr Moon says: Why was it delayed?
Anthony says: Hecny says flights from Da Nang were pushed back after the typhoon. I have asked them to confirm this in writing.
Mr Moon says: Will there be extra cost?
Anthony says: No email has mentioned any cost so far. I'd like to highlight that this is not confirmed yet.
Mr Moon says: Who is following up?
Anthony says: Ms Trinh Do is handling the booking and the truck. I will update you as soon as the cargo is accepted at the terminal.
Mr Moon says: Good. Please also tell me if the buyer asks for a claim.
Anthony says: Yes, sir. I will let you know right away.
Now repeat the two key sentences.
The first sentence. I have asked them to confirm this in writing. ... ... ... One more time. I have asked them to confirm this in writing. ... ... ...
The second sentence. I will update you as soon as the cargo is accepted at the terminal. ... ... ... One more time. I will update you as soon as the cargo is accepted at the terminal. ... ... ...
Part seven. Weak word practice.
Your coach said the sentence frames were all used, but the subject and verb inside them often broke. So let's fix three sentences from Saturday's test. Listen, then repeat the correct one.

The first one uses until. After until, use the present tense. Please hold off on the order until head office confirms. ... ... ... One more time. Please hold off on the order until head office confirms. ... ... ...

The second one needs a subject after if. If the documents are not ready by Friday, we will have to delay the shipment. ... ... ... One more time. If the documents are not ready by Friday, we will have to delay the shipment. ... ... ...

The third one keeps normal word order after the frame. Is there any way the warehouse can send me the stock list by this afternoon? ... ... ... One more time. Is there any way the warehouse can send me the stock list by this afternoon? ... ... ...
Now three more words from the test. A dedicated team means a team that does only this work. Please ask the supplier for a dedicated team. ... ... ...
Confirm receipt means to say that you received something. Please confirm receipt of the passport copy. ... ... ...
Prioritize is the verb. Priority is the noun. Please prioritize the Vince shipment today. ... ... ...
Part eight. Closing.
Here is the one thing to do today. Make sure the Vince boxes reach the air terminal before today's cut-off, and get the delay reason in writing.
After that, open the physical count file and prepare your short report to Mr Moon. Then send Mai one message with one deadline.
That is all for today, Anthony. Have a good Tuesday. See you tomorrow.
